items.title: Support one-shot authenticated calls without persisting a login (env-provided token)
items.body:
# Support one-shot authenticated calls without persisting a login (env-provided token)

## Use case

Agentic CI workflows that mint short-lived, narrowly-scoped tokens per
session/task (self-hosted Forgejo 15, `tea` 0.16.0). The agent obtains a
credential with exactly the scope a track needs, uses it, and it expires —
the human authorizes once, the agent never persists anything to disk.

## Gap

Today every operating command (`tea api`, `tea pulls`, …) authenticates
exclusively via stored logins. `$GITEA_SERVER_TOKEN` only feeds
`logins add --token`, which persists the login to config — so a token cannot
be *used* without writing it to disk first. There is no global `--token`
flag and no other command honors the env var (checked `tea api -h` and the
top-level help on 0.16.0).

Consequence: a per-session ephemeral token must either be persisted
(`logins add` + `logins delete`, which still leaves the DB token live until
a password-authenticated DELETE) or the workflow falls back to rotating a
standing login — both weaker than true env-only operation.

## Request

Honor an env-provided (or global `--token`) credential for single
invocations without creating/persisting a login entry, e.g. read order:
explicit flag > env var > stored login. Failing that, document that
diskless operation is unsupported so automation authors stop trying.

Out of scope here: token TTL (server-side matter, tracked separately —
upstream tokens carry no expiry field at all).

items.title: Bug: SSH login fails when REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW is true
items.body:
### describe your environment
- tea version used (`tea -v`): 0.16.0
    - [ ] I also reproduced the issue [with the latest main build](https://dl.gitea.com/tea/main/)
- Gitea version used: 1.27.3
    - [ ] the issue only occurred after updating gitea recently
- operating system: Linux
- I make use of...
    - [ ] non-standard default branch names (no `main`,`master`, or `trunk`)
    - [ ] .ssh/config or .gitconfig host aliases in my git remotes
    - [x] ssh_agent or similar
    - [ ] non-standard ports for gitea and/or ssh
    - [ ] something else that's likely to interact badly with tea: ...


Please provide the output of `git remote -v` (if the issue is related to tea not finding resources on Gitea):
```

```

### describe the issue (observed vs expected behaviour)

When `REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW` is set to `true` the `/api/v1/version` endpoint is inaccessible unless logged in. Tea will attempt to check the servers version number before singing the request with the chosen ssh key. This causes the version request to return a 403 causing the tea login process to fail.
